findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct AC3's premise: user_data.sh DOES assert /var/gerrit mounted (require_mounted / ASSERT-MOUNT-TOOK inside mount_ebs_volume at user_data.sh:180, with a FATAL exit at 192-195). Re-scope AC3 to the real gap — the assertion only runs on first boot, so a stop/start does not re-verify — and drop the 'nothing asserts this' claim.
evidence: Plan AC3: 'Nothing in `user_data.sh` asserts this (see `unamused-cloudy-junebug`), so a silently-skipped `nofail` mount would leave Gerrit on the root filesystem undetected.'
user_data.sh:192-195 wraps the /var/gerrit mount: `if ! mount_ebs_volume "${data_volume_id}" /var/gerrit; then echo "FATAL: ... refusing to run Gerrit on the ROOT filesystem"; exit 1`
user_data.sh:180 `require_mounted "$mount_point" || return 4 # ASSERT-MOUNT-TOOK` inside mount_ebs_volume

user_data.sh:186-209 comment: 'mount_ebs_volume now asserts the mount took, so this branch covers the silent nofail skip ... EVERY volume gets it ... which is how /var/gerrit came to have no assertion at all'
findings.finding: AC3's premise that 'Nothing in user_data.sh asserts /var/gerrit is mounted' is refuted by the current code.
scenarios: Operator reads AC3, adds a redundant /var/gerrit assertion that already exists, or mis-scopes the verification believing the boot-time assert is absent
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite AC3 to: 'user_data.sh asserts /var/gerrit mounted at boot (FATAL exit, user_data.sh:192-195), but that assert runs once-per-instance and a stop/start will not re-run it; independently verify /var/gerrit is mounted AFTER the instance cycle.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify AC6's check concretely and reconcile it with existing mechanisms: whether it extends `scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` (which already joins Terraform attachments vs host mounts for the S1 volume shape), consumes `terraform-drift.yml`'s `-detailed-exitcode` (exit 2 = declared-but-unprovisioned, the S2 alarm shape), and/or adds only the net-new surface (e.g. a CloudWatch alarm-existence probe) rather than a new full comparator.
evidence: AC6 text: 'A CHECK exists that distinguishes "declared in Terraform" from "provisioned in AWS", so the S1/S2 shape cannot recur silently.'

scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py docstring already implements this join: 'Terraform holds one half (which volumes are attached)... the host holds the other... This script performs that join and fails loudly' — exactly the S1 gate-scratch shape.
scripts/check_terraform_tree_currency.py docstring cites the S2 shape directly: 'five CloudWatch alarms declared on main did not exist in AWS' while the stale plan read '0 to add'.
.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml runs live `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` where exit 2 = un-applied declaration / drift; the plan itself calls this workflow 'the natural home'.
AC6 does not state whether it extends assert_volumes_in_service.py, consumes the drift plan's exit code, adds an alarm-existence probe, or builds a new comparator.
findings.finding: AC6 requires a 'CHECK that distinguishes declared in Terraform from provisioned in AWS' but never specifies what it is or how it relates to three closely-adjacent existing mechanisms, creating a concrete NIH/rebuild risk.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria → AC6; Verification bullet 'The declared-vs-provisioned check is a code change'
scenarios: Author writes a fourth Terraform-vs-AWS comparator that re-derives the volume/attachment join already in assert_volumes_in_service.py.
Author re-implements a live-plan/describe comparison that terraform-drift.yml's exit-2 signal already provides.
findings.suggested_fix: Note that the S1 shape (attached-but-unmounted volume) is already covered by scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py, and that the S2 shape (alarm declared, absent in AWS) is what terraform-drift.yml's non-empty plan detects; scope AC6 to the smallest gap not already covered (e.g. an alarm-existence assertion that runs independently of the drift workflow's fmt-check defect) and reuse the existing join/plan rather than rebuilding it.
